detail.abstract:
Bitcoin's design encodes four hard consensus-rule constraints: a fixed per-block weight ceiling, a geometrically decaying block subsidy, an open profit-driven mining market, and a digital signature scheme vulnerable to future cryptographically-relevant quantum computers (CRQCs). This paper develops twelve original quantitative constructions on top of these four constraints, spanning bulk-service queueing theory, coupled dynamical systems, Tullock contest theory, reinforced-dynamics stability analysis, entropy diagnostics, stochastic first-passage theory, competing-risk survival analysis, and inequality theory.
The central technical result is a Conditional Trilemma Boundary, formulated as an explicit dichotomy rather than an unconditional claim. Under a stated, falsifiable assumption—that the fee market's per-transaction ceiling does not scale with Bitcoin's market value—the best-case security-to-value ratio achievable through transaction fees decays toward zero as market capitalization grows, and the decentralization ceiling remains flat rather than expanding with adoption once the block subsidy decays to a negligible share of miner revenue. Under the complementary, equally plausible assumption—that Bitcoin increasingly settles higher average economic value per on-chain transaction as blockspace is rationed across a growing economy—neither conclusion holds: the decentralization ceiling rises with adoption and the security-to-value ratio stabilizes.
Which regime the network actually occupies is an open empirical question regarding fee-market elasticity rather than a property derivable from consensus constants alone. Quantitative parameters are sourced against 2026 data (mining-pool telemetry, the Cambridge Bitcoin Electricity Consumption Index, mempool fee reporting, and the active specifications of BIP-360 and BIP-361) or explicitly evaluated across sensitivity ranges. The paper concludes with counterarguments and structural mitigations—including Layer-2 scaling and miner-led template construction protocols such as Stratum V2—highlighting that protocol constraints define systemic economic pressures rather than predetermined outcomes.

detail.abstract: This study applies a goal-based Markov chain and Monte Carlo simulation model to predict match outcomes (win, draw or loss) in Liga MX, a professional soccer league in Mexico which has received little attention in sports analytics literature compared to other competitive soccer leagues, primarily the English Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, and Bundesliga. Team-specific home and away scoring and conceding rates were calculated from the complete 2025-2026 Liga MX season (304 regular-season games) to simulate thousands of matchups via random draws from Poisson Distribution. The model was tested against home-field baseline and a ranking-based on baseline across 3 experiments: an in-sample evaluation, a chronological train/test split, and a prospective forecast applied to real matches from the following season. Our findings show that the Monte Carlo model outperformed the home-field baseline in two of three experiments, but the simpler ranking baseline matched or outperformed it in two of three experiments as well. Accuracy dropped under the train/test split, consistent with overfitting, but recovered under the prospective forecast. These results suggest that goal-based modeling generalized to Liga MX, while also revealing greater team-to-team variation in home-field advantage than prior research has reported.

title: Green Subsidies and Green Consumption: Bunching at an Appliance Rebate Cap
affiliations: Renmin University of China, Renmin University of China, Zhongnan University of Economics and Law, Renmin University of China and Zhongnan University of Economics and Law

detail.title: Green Subsidies and Green Consumption: Bunching at an Appliance Rebate Cap
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of a non-linear green subsidy on energy-efficient home appliance purchases. Using a bunching estimator and air conditioner transaction data from Beijing, China, between 2016 and 2019, we identify localized price distortions induced by a maximum subsidy cap, which creates a convex budget kink. This cap leads to a 0.60% intensive-margin decrease in average transaction prices. We estimate an empirical equilibrium expenditure elasticity of 0.231, indicating that sellers and consumers adjust prices and choices modestly to diluted financial incentives above the cap. A structural calibration reveals that the policy generates an average incremental consumer surplus of 776.19 RMB per transaction alongside a minimal deadweight loss of just 4.05 RMB. This exceptionally low efficiency cost establishes a highly attainable break-even threshold for the program's unpriced environmental benefits. Finally, mechanism tests and subgroup analyses demonstrate that the equilibrium policy distortion is overwhelmingly driven by demand-side consumer sorting, with behavioral responses remaining structurally uniform across demographic segments.

detail.abstract: This research investigates the dynamics of U.S. startups that developed and produced artificial intelligence (AI) between 2013 and 2024, analyzing the impact of Corporate Venture Capital (CVC) and Independent Venture Capital (IVC or VC) investors on startups that had already received at least one Series A investment. The results show that the presence of CVC and IVC contributes to a higher probability of mergers and acquisitions (M&A), suggesting that both corporate and independent capital play a relevant role in determining firms' exit routes. However, unlike part of the literature, no solid evidence was found that these investors help startups remain in the market longer while seeking new rounds (follow on), pointing to the existence of additional factors that may influence the decision to continue raising funds or pursue a strategic exit.

detail.abstract: This technical report provides an analysis of the research study investigating the determinants of exit events - specifically Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) and Initial Public Offerings (IPO) - in the Brazilian fintech ecosystem. The study is based on the premise that, although fintechs represent a disruptive force and a pillar of innovation and financial inclusion in Brazil, their trajectories are permeated by challenges that culminate in the need for liquidity events for founders and investors. The central objective of the research is therefore to discern how a set of factors, divided between characteristics intrinsic to the firms and conditions in the macroeconomic environment, influences the time until an M&A or IPO occurs. To this end, a survival analysis methodology was employed, using a parametric regression model with a Lognormal distribution on a sample of 625 Brazilian fintechs, whose data were extracted from the Crunchbase platform. The variables analyzed range from the firm's investment history, founder characteristics, and location to a set of key macroeconomic indicators. The research results are striking and reveal a predominance of exogenous over endogenous factors. Specifically, a scenario of declining interest rates (SELIC) and a lower Ibovespa index acts as a strong accelerator of these events, increasing the rate by more than threefold and twofold, respectively. By contrast, an environment of low default rates on corporate credit and low technology costs delays the occurrence of M&A or IPO. Among the internal factors, the only variable that remained significant in the final model was the strategy of making acquisitions, which proved to be a factor that accelerates the pursuit of an exit event. The study contributes to the literature by mapping the forces governing the final stages of the startup life cycle in Brazil.

detail.abstract: Renewable-origin certificates compress differences in temporal matching, spatial matching and additionality into a low-value commodity attribute. We quantify the value left unrecognised when higher-quality on-site renewable consumption is valued only against this benchmark. The empirical application combines official solar statistics, regional weather and representative nondomestic building loads in Great Britain for 2025. A stratified capacity reconstruction gives a central building-associated PV proxy of 2.929 GW, with selected scenarios of 1.832 to 4.026 GW. The central model produces 3.081 TWh and matches 3.081 TWh within regional building classes at half-hour resolution. Quality-valuation scenarios imply a central difference of £6.00 per matched MWh above the REGO benchmark. Applied to the central quantity, this gives an annual owner opportunity of £18.494 million under full attribute retention. Separate financing and carbon appraisals identify different private and public consequences of the same electricity use. The contribution is to express quality differentiation in money and show its scale within an existing renewable asset population. Building-associated PV supplies the quantitative application. The argument extends to other on-site renewable arrangements, including potentially larger applications at data centres. Recognising consumption quality would give owners a basis for capturing value that a simple origin price leaves out.

detail.abstract: The study investigates the influence of macroeconomic factors and financial market structure on startup funding amounts in Latin America between 2011 and 2022. Using a dynamic panel methodology, the research analyzes data from Crunchbase, the World Bank, and central banks to estimate the impact of variables such as interest rates and country risk on the financing of firms at the Pre-seed, Seed, and Series A stages. The most significant results indicate negative temporal dependence in the amounts raised, suggesting mean reversion in investments. In addition, the interest rate showed a distinct impact depending on the startup stage: a positive or null effect at early stages and a negative effect, consistent with economic theory, at the Series A stage. The study has limitations, such as the annual frequency of the data and the small number of observations, which may affect the precision of the coefficients. The main conclusion is that, although most macroeconomic variables were not statistically significant, the temporal dynamics of investment and the role of the interest rate are crucial to the startup ecosystem in the region.

title: MoCo-cDDPM: A Latent Conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Framework for Retrospective Motion Artifact Correction in 3D MRI

detail.title: MoCo-cDDPM: A Latent Conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Framework for Retrospective Motion Artifact Correction in 3D MRI
detail.abstract: Motion artifacts are a prevalent issue across many medical imaging modalities. In particular, the long acquisition times required for Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) make patients susceptible to movement, leading to ghosting, blurring, and other motion-related artifacts. Severe motion can significantly degrade image quality and compromise diagnostic interpretation. While deep learning-based techniques have been developed in recent years to mitigate this issue, they remain largely limited to 2D images and traditional CNN-based architectures. Diffusion models have recently shown strong performance in medical image generation and restoration tasks. In this paper, we propose MoCo-cDDPM, a novel latent space diffusion-based model designed to correct motion artifacts in volumetric 3D brain MRI data. The proposed method comprises a three-stage deep learning framework. First, 3D MRI volumes are mapped to a latent space using a Vector-Quantized Generative Adversarial Network (VQGAN), which significantly reduces the computational overhead of the subsequent diffusion model. Next, the diffusion model is pre-trained on clean, motion-free MRI volumes to learn the distribution of anatomically plausible brain images. Finally, the pre-trained model is conditioned on paired simulated motion-corrupted and ground-truth volumes to learn artifact correction during inference. We evaluated MoCo-cDDPM on real-world motion-corrupted data and compared its performance with established deep learning models. MoCo-cDDPM increased the mean SSIM from 0.8528 to 0.9004 and reduced the LPIPS from 0.1560 to 0.1051 (both p < 0.001) in the severe motion cohort, successfully retaining anatomical details from motion-affected images
